next_probe_tests.procedure: Construct a finite model in which an interested actor retains genuine post-observation acceptance discretion, while every allowed exercise preserves equal probabilities conditional on all relevant histories. Determine whether a procedural complaint remains without hidden bias or distributional change.

next_probe_tests.test: Source map: lottery and fair chances
next_probe_tests.procedure: Retrieve and read closest primary accounts of lotteries and fair chances. Compare whether fairness is defined by equal chance, equal claim treatment, procedural legitimacy, or a combination.
next_probe_tests.failure_signal: If the intended literature treats the issue as exhausted by equal chances, narrow the thesis to institutional reliability or set it aside.

next_probe_tests.test: Source map: procedural equality and discretionary power
next_probe_tests.procedure: Read primary sources on procedural equality, arbitrary power/non-domination, and public commitment. Identify whether post-draw contestability adds a distinct condition or merely tracks distributional risk.
next_probe_tests.failure_signal: If no independent procedural premise is defensible, remove the status argument.

next_probe_tests.failure_signal: Any calculation error undermines the worked case; any deviation that preserves all relevant probabilities becomes a direct test of the status claim.
